# rTFT: hazard models for thermal failure time data

`rTFT` fits discrete-time survival models to the times at which
individual organisms fail under thermal exposure (e.g., loss of
equilibrium, knockdown or death), using Bayesian inference in
[Stan](https://mc-stan.org) through
[brms](https://paulbuerkner.com/brms/). The hazard is the product of a
failure rate that depends on temperature, following [Kingsolver and
Umbanhowar (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1242/jeb.167858), and a baseline
that may depend on the time under exposure.

Thermal tolerance is usually reported as a summary of an assay, such as
the critical thermal maximum (CTmax) of a ramping trial or the time to
failure at a constant temperature. These summaries depend on how the
assay was run (e.g., the ramp rate or the temperatures chosen). In
`rTFT`, a model is fitted to the failure times themselves (available in
both types of assays), and the usual summaries are derived from the
fitted model, each with its posterior uncertainty.

With the package, one can:

- fit failure times that are exact, interval-censored or both, from
  static assays, ramping assays or both, with any of several functions
  for the failure rate and for the baseline;
- let the failure rate depend on covariates (e.g., body mass), on
  group-level effects (e.g., trials) and on other stressors (e.g.,
  dissolved oxygen);
- check the fit of a model against the data;
- derive static and dynamic critical thermal maxima, thermal death time
  curves and thermal tolerance landscapes;
- compare models by cross-validation that leaves out whole individuals
  or trials, and average them;
- predict survival along a record of temperature (e.g., a stream during
  a heat wave), and of any co-stressors recorded with it.

## Installation

`rTFT` is installed from GitHub.

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("eogmartins/rTFT", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

Fitting a model requires a working installation of Stan, through either
`cmdstanr` or `rstan` (see the [installation notes of
brms](https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms#how-do-i-install-brms)).
`cmdstanr` is recommended and was used to fit the models of the
vignettes. It can be asked for with `backend = "cmdstanr"` in
[`fit_hazard()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/fit_hazard.md).

Building the vignettes requires [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

## Example

Three simulated datasets are included with the package: a static assay
(`static_assay`), a ramping assay run at two levels of dissolved oxygen
(`ramp_assay`) and a record of stream temperature (`stream_record`).
They were simulated from a known model, so that what a model estimates
can be compared with the values used in the simulation.

The example below uses `static_assay`, which contains the times to loss
of equilibrium of 120 juvenile salmonids held at 23, 25 or 27°C and
checked every hour for five days. It shows the four steps of an
analysis, which the vignette *Getting started with rTFT* describes in
detail.

``` r

library(rTFT)

# 1. The table of intervals at risk, built from the temperature of each treatment
#    through time and the times of the checks.
path   <- data.frame(path_id = rep(c("T23", "T25", "T27"), each = 2),
                     time    = rep(c(0, 7200), times = 3),
                     temp    = rep(c(23, 25, 27), each = 2))
checks <- expand.grid(path_id = c("T23", "T25", "T27"), time = seq(0, 7200, by = 60))
long   <- build_hazard_data(static_assay, path, observation = "interval",
                            covariates = c("mass", "trial"), checks = checks)

# 2. An exponential failure rate with a Weibull baseline, with the failure rate
#    depending on body mass and varying among trials.
fit <- fit_hazard(long, m_form = "exp", baseline = "weibull",
                  dpar_formulas = list(loga = ~ 1 + I(mass - 15) + (1 | trial)),
                  chains = 4, cores = 4, backend = "cmdstanr")

# 3. The static critical thermal maximum for an exposure of 60 min and the thermal
#    death time curves of a 15 g fish.
tol <- derive_tdt_ttl(fit, newdata = data.frame(mass = 15), t_ref = 60)
tol$sctmax
plot_tdt(tol, time_unit = "min")

# 4. Survival along 30 days of hourly stream temperature.
pred <- predict_survival(fit, stream_record, newdata = data.frame(mass = 15))
plot_survival(pred, temperature = TRUE)
```

## Vignettes

Four vignettes describe the package, and are best read in this order.
They can be read, with the help pages, on the [website of the
package](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/).

1.  *Getting started with rTFT*
    ([`vignette("getting-started", package = "rTFT")`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/articles/getting-started.md)):
    the model, a static assay, the checks of a fitted model, the derived
    quantities and a prediction of survival along a record of stream
    temperature.
2.  *Ramping assays*
    ([`vignette("ramping-assays", package = "rTFT")`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/articles/ramping-assays.md)):
    how a ramp is given to the package, the dynamic critical thermal
    maximum, and what the choice of ramp rates allows a model to
    estimate.
3.  *Comparing and averaging models*
    ([`vignette("comparing-and-averaging-models", package = "rTFT")`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/articles/comparing-and-averaging-models.md)):
    cross-validation by individual or trial, model weights and averaged
    predictions.
4.  *Temperature and a co-stressor*
    ([`vignette("temperature-and-a-co-stressor", package = "rTFT")`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/articles/temperature-and-a-co-stressor.md)):
    dissolved oxygen as a second stressor, with and without an
    interaction with temperature.

## Getting help

Problems and suggestions can be reported at
<https://github.com/eogmartins/rTFT/issues>.

## Citation

If you use the package, please cite it as:

> Martins, E. G. (2026). rTFT: hazard models for thermal failure time
> data. R package version 0.1.0. <https://github.com/eogmartins/rTFT>

The same reference is given by `citation("rTFT")`.

## Use of generative AI

The code, tests and documentation of this package were drafted with the
assistance of Claude (Anthropic), used through Claude Code (models Opus
4.8–5.5 and Fable 5.1). The author specified the models, their
parameterisation and the quantities derived from them, reviewed each
function and its tests before they entered the package, and takes
responsibility for its content.

# Package index

## Fitting

Building the table of intervals at risk from the failure times and the
temperature of each trial, and fitting the model.

- [`build_hazard_data()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/build_hazard_data.md)
  : Build the row-per-interval table a failure-rate model is fitted to
- [`ramp_path()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/ramp_path.md)
  : Build a linear ramp temperature trajectory
- [`assess_ramp_linearity()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/assess_ramp_linearity.md)
  : Assess how linear a logged temperature trace is
- [`fit_hazard()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/fit_hazard.md)
  : Fit a failure-rate hazard model with brms
- [`costressor()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/costressor.md)
  : Declare a co-stressor for a failure-rate hazard model
- [`build_hazard_prior()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/build_hazard_prior.md)
  : Weakly-informative default priors for a failure-rate hazard model
- [`M_catalogue`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/M_catalogue.md)
  : Failure rate functions M(T)
- [`h0_catalogue`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/h0_catalogue.md)
  : Baseline hazard functions h0(tau)

## Checking a fitted model

- [`check_survival()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/check_survival.md)
  : Check a fitted model against the survival observed in each group
- [`plot_check()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/plot_check.md)
  : Plot the check of a fitted model against observed survival
- [`hazard_residuals()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/hazard_residuals.md)
  : Residuals of a fitted model, one per individual
- [`plot_residuals()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/plot_residuals.md)
  : Plot the residuals of a fitted model

## Derived quantities

Critical thermal maxima, thermal death time curves and thermal tolerance
landscapes, each with its posterior uncertainty.

- [`derive_tdt_ttl()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/derive_tdt_ttl.md)
  : Thermal tolerance derived from a fitted failure-rate model
- [`derive_dctmax()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/derive_dctmax.md)
  : Dynamic critical thermal maximum under a ramp, from a fitted model
- [`plot_tdt()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/plot_tdt.md)
  : Plot the thermal death time curves
- [`plot_ttl()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/plot_ttl.md)
  : Plot the thermal tolerance landscape
- [`plot_ttl_3d()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/plot_ttl_3d.md)
  : Plot the thermal tolerance landscape as a surface to rotate
- [`M_draws()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/M_draws.md)
  : The fitted failure rate over temperature, for each posterior draw

## Comparing and averaging models

- [`loo_hazard()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/loo_hazard.md)
  : Leave-one-out cross-validation that leaves out whole individuals or
  groups
- [`kfold_hazard()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/kfold_hazard.md)
  : Cross-validation by refitting, leaving out whole individuals or
  groups
- [`hazard_weights()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/hazard_weights.md)
  : Weights for averaging failure-rate models
- [`average_tdt_ttl()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/average_tdt_ttl.md)
  : Thermal tolerance averaged over several fitted models
- [`average_dctmax()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/average_dctmax.md)
  : Dynamic critical thermal maximum averaged over several fitted models
- [`average_survival()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/average_survival.md)
  : Survival along a record of temperature, averaged over several fitted
  models

## Predicting survival

- [`predict_survival()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/predict_survival.md)
  : Survival along a record of temperature, from a fitted failure-rate
  model
- [`plot_survival()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/plot_survival.md)
  : Plot survival along a record of temperature
- [`plot_risk()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/plot_risk.md)
  : Plot each period's share of the risk along a record

## Data

Simulated datasets used in the help pages and the vignettes.

- [`static_assay`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/static_assay.md)
  : A simulated static assay of thermal tolerance
- [`ramp_assay`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/ramp_assay.md)
  : A simulated ramping assay of thermal tolerance, with two levels of
  oxygen
- [`stream_record`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/stream_record.md)
  : A simulated record of stream temperature

## Building blocks

The pieces that
[`fit_hazard()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/fit_hazard.md)
and the derived quantities are assembled from. Most analyses do not call
them directly.

- [`build_hazard_spec()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/build_hazard_spec.md)
  : Assemble the brms formula and family for a failure-rate hazard model
- [`brms_log_M`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/brms_log_M.md)
  : log M(T) for each failure rate function, as a brms expression string
- [`brms_log_h0`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/brms_log_h0.md)
  : log h0(tau) for each baseline function, as a brms expression string
- [`H0_of()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/H0_of.md) :
  The cumulative baseline hazard of a given shape
- [`H0inv_of()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/H0inv_of.md)
  : The inverse of the cumulative baseline hazard
- [`cloglog_bern_family()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/cloglog_bern_family.md)
  : Complementary log-log Bernoulli response, on the identity link
- [`hazard_mixed_family()`](https://eogmartins.github.io/rTFT/reference/hazard_mixed_family.md)
  : Response distribution for a table mixing interval-censored and
  known-time failures
